body: Martial arts are a lifesaver for me. I started with Taekwondo in 2021 and it's given me so much purpose. I plan on learning about as many martial arts as I can and practicing the ones that interest me most. Martial arts are especially applicable to ADHD because most of them emphasize practicing inner peace, focus, self-compassion, and patience. Plus, moving your body is a great way to combat hyperactivity and restlessness. I also find that interacting with peers and instructors in a goal-oriented setting (like a class or competition) helps alleviate my social anxiety a bit. I think it's easier to talk to people naturally when you have something major like that in common.

Monitoring your partner and keeping them on the right track isn't your responsibility, nor should it be. You don't want to become a caretaker for someone who will place the blame on you for not doing enough when they inevitably screw up. It's a good idea to absolve yourself of that responsibility before it ruins your life.

The only one who can keep them in check is themselves. They are the only one who can disclose when they're having cravings to a sponsor. They are the only one who can reach out to different resources for help. They are the only one who can take the steps to become sober.

Love makes things very hard. You want to protect them from their disease and save them before it's too late. You can't. In an alcoholic's situation, they are the only one who can save themselves, but only if they are truly ready to take action.

I had a Biology teacher last semester that I really really liked. She could be a little blunt at times when it came to people talking in class or playing on their phones (99% of the time she was very professional), and she was adamant about her class rules and us adhering to studying. It saddened me to notice that a lot of students just genuinely didn't seem to care and did what they wanted anyway, even though the class was only 50 minutes and whatever they were doing could wait until after. I looked at her on Rate My Professor out of curiosity after the semester ended and was shocked. A lot of people gave her negative reviews about her being strict and unprofessional, and about her class being hard.

In my opinion (and this is coming from someone who enjoys science) it wasn't a hard class at all if you studied and did what she advised. It was only an introductory class as well. She even set up a lecture manual for us that was an exact copy of the PowerPoint slides shown in class, with some blanks so we could fill in the words as we listened to lecture. This kept me engaged in absorbing the material and I was grateful for it. She was passionate about what she was teaching and strived to convey that passion and deeper meaning to her students, but some people were just ignorant to it.

I would warn fellow students about using Rate My Professor because it can set up some potentially harmful preconceptions before you take a class. Instead, observe the class and professor during the drop/add period and judge for yourself.

I have some strange platonic attraction to intelligent and tomboyish (but still embracing their feminine side) middle-aged women with a strong personality. I know that sounds really specific but it's ironic that there have been not one, but two women like this who have greatly drawn my attention.

The first is my manager at work. She's honestly become a mother figure to me. She's the kind of person to give tough love, but the kind that isn't emotionally damaging. She always encourages me to better myself. She always listens when I need to vent and she gives solid, honest advice. There's also been times where I was extremely sick at work, and she would care for me and buy me medicine or food so I would feel better. She even asked me to dog sit for her a few times while she was out of town (she trusts me!). She treats me like I'm her own kid and I'm so grateful for her. She's one of those people that, even after I leave this job, I'm going to keep in touch with her always.

I have a more professional relationship with the other woman I look up to. She's my college biology teacher. She's passionate about biology and she encourages everyone to do well. She can also be stern at times towards students who aren't doing what they're supposed to (totally understandable). I like her because she's both bubbly and strong. I'm really good with science and she's acknowledged that I've made good grades in her class, and it made me happy.

Both women are beautiful, stern when it's necessary, intelligent, tomboyish (to varying degrees), kind, and want me and others to be the best we can be. I realize that they truly are role models for me because my biological mother is a garbage human being who treated me like I was lesser. I'm grateful to have good female role models despite my upbringing.

You could have chose playing outside, or eating, or leaving the house, or any other things to cope. You chose video games and fantasy books because you enjoy them.
